subject: Brandt's bat
title: A Bat Lighter Than a Grape Lived 41 Years in the Wild

scenes.text: This bat weighs about as much as two grapes. It can outlive a horse.
In 1964, scientists put a band on a Brandt's bat in a Siberian cave.
In 2005 they caught the same bat again. It was at least forty-one years old.
For its size, no mammal studied lives longer. Lab mice, which are bigger, rarely live past three.
Its genes hold a clue: changes to growth hormone receptors, the same kind that double lifespan in lab mice.
And long winters of hibernation slow it down even more. Small, cold and patient wins.

description:
A Brandt's bat weighing about 4 to 8 grams, banded in Siberia in 1964 and recaptured in 2005, was at least 41 years old, the oldest bat on record according to Guinness World Records.
Its genome shows changes in growth hormone and IGF1 receptor genes, which in mice are linked to longer lives and smaller bodies.
Which small animal would you guess lives longest?
first_comment: Bigger animals usually live longer, but bats break the rule. Which animal do you think lives longest for its size?
